subject: Urgent: Brightline production latency + error surge after SDK update
messages:
From: Jack Meyers <jack@brightline.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency + 5xx spike after SDK 1.8.2 (prod)

Monica / Redwood team,

We pushed the client SDK v1.8.2 into our checkout microservice last night (canary -> prod) and are now seeing a ~4-5x latency increase for streaming completions and an uptick in 502/503 errors. Error rate went from ~0.3% to 4.7% within the hour after the deploy. See the attached PCAP and a short debug trace (redwood_debug_trace.txt).

Key findings from our side: 
- Failures only when using streaming responses with our long-poll aggregator.
- Logs show repeated "streaming-decorator: trailer mismatch" followed by connection reset.
- Errors appear correlated with longer prompt prefixes (>1.2k tokens).

This is high-severity for us: impacts checkout throughput and we’re seeing cart abandonment. Can you triage immediately? We need either a mitigation or rollback guidance within the next 2 hours.

Thanks,
Jack
Lead SRE, Brightline
Attachments: integration_packet_capture.pcap, redwood_debug_trace.txt
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jack Meyers <jack@brightline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx spike after SDK 1.8.2 (prod)

Jack — thanks for the quick heads-up and the artifacts. We’re on this now.

Immediate plan:
- I’ve looped in Eng for a hotfix investigation (Jonas Weber).
- Marissa (CS) will coordinate status updates to your team and slack channel.
- Can you confirm whether you have request sampling enabled (X-RW-Trace) and share a few raw request IDs? That will help trace across our serving runtime.

Workaround for short term: if possible, avoid using streaming responses for the checkout route (switch to non-streaming completion or pin the SDK to v1.8.1). If you want, we can issue a temporary configuration at the edge to fallback to non-streaming for that route while we investigate.

I’ll update in 30–45 minutes.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx spike after SDK 1.8.2 (prod)

Monica / Marissa — quick triage notes from Eng: 

Observed symptoms: 
- The traces show response frames where the "trailer" headers are emitted split across two TCP frames. Our streaming decorator assumes trailer headers are delivered atomically and the recent SDK change moved to a smaller internal write buffer (v1.8.2). In some client-network interactions, the trailer header bytes are split, leading our parser to treat the partial header as payload and then fail validation when the remainder arrives — resulting in a trailer mismatch and connection abort.

Immediate mitigation options we can push right now: 
1) Server-side tolerant parse: accept split trailer header sequences for the next 24–48 hours (config flag) — low risk, quick toggle but requires a canary rollout.
2) Edge fallback: route the affected customer route to non-streaming model variant (no trailers) — instant but higher cost and latency overhead for other customers.
3) Recommend Brightline pin SDK to v1.8.1 or use the header-reassembly workaround in their SDK config (we can provide a build with buffer size bumped).

We can prepare a canary release of a parser fix (handling split trailer tokens) within ~6 hours. If exec wants aggressive mitigation, option #1 + customer pin would minimize impact while we land the fix.

Attaching quick log excerpts and proposed parser patch diff in Jira: JIRA-INC-9132.

—Jonas
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jack Meyers <jack@brightline.com>, Brightline Engineering <eng@brightline.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx spike after SDK 1.8.2 (prod) — short-term mitigation

Jack / team — update and recommended next steps: 

What we did: 
- Rolled a config to make the parser tolerant of split trailer headers in a small canary (internal id: canary-rw-242). Initial canary reduced 5xxs by ~85% for similar long-prefix traffic.
- Produced an interim SDK hotfix that increases the client write buffer (v1.8.2-patch1) — this avoids producing split trailer writes from the client side; we attached the build and instructions.

Recommended immediate path: 
1) Brightline: Apply the SDK patch (v1.8.2-patch1) to the checkout service canary. This should be the fastest mitigation if you can deploy.
2) Redwood: Keep parser-tolerance flag enabled for 48 hours while we validate across regions.

Next actions and asks from Brightline: 
- Can you share 3 request IDs where you still see errors after applying the SDK patch (if any)?
- Procurement/proc team: Jonas has flagged this for an RCA and possible SLA credit discussion; please escalate internally if needed.

I will set up a 30-minute sync for 10:30 PT to walk through the patch and timeline. Rishi will follow up on commercial implications.

Attachments: redwood_1.8.2-patch1-instructions.txt

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jack Meyers <jack@brightline.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Brightline Engineering <eng@brightline.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx spike after SDK 1.8.2 (prod) — short-term mitigation

Monica / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. We applied v1.8.2-patch1 to the canary and saw stream error rates drop immediately; overall latency returned to expected levels for the sampled requests.

Two requests: 
1) We need a written RCA and timeline for the permanent parser patch. Our legal/procurement team will also request the results for the SLA credit review.
2) Please confirm whether this issue could have impacted historical request logs (we rely on your ingestion for analytics). If so, what windows should we consider suspect?

We’ll join the 10:30 PT sync. Appreciate the swift engagement.

—Jack
Lead SRE, Brightline
